Fit the Poisson survival model on summed cells

dot-fit_survival_cells.Rd

The fit shared by both methods of fit_survival_model(). Fits one model per exit type, with log(exposure) as an offset and fixed effects for tenure band (and calendar year if period_effects). An exit type no one had cannot be fitted, so it is left out with a warning.

Usage

.fit_survival_cells(
  cells,
  panel,
  covariate_cols,
  exit_types,
  band_width,
  period_effects,
  make_tidy_output,
  ...
)

Arguments

cells

A data.table of cells with exit counts (exit_retired, exit_other), years at risk (exposure), tenure band (.band), snapshot (.ref) and covariate_cols. Modified by reference: sorted, and a .year column is added.

panel

The survival_panel the cells were summed from, for the column names it remembers.

covariate_cols

Character vector. The covariates to model, or empty for tenure (and year) effects only.

exit_types

Character vector. Any of "retired" and "other".

band_width

Number. The width of the tenure bands, in years.

period_effects

Logical. Whether to add calendar year fixed effects.

make_tidy_output

Logical. Whether to return the table of hazard ratios from tidy.survival_model() instead of the model.

...

Further arguments passed to fixest::fepois(), already checked by .check_survival_model_args().

Value

A survival_model: the output of fixest::fepois() (a fixest_multi with one model per exit type, or a fixest if only one is fitted) with class survival_model prepended, and two attributes for predict.survival_model(): cells (the cells it was fitted on) and survival_settings (the panel's columns, band_width, period_effects, the exit types asked for and those no one had). Or, if make_tidy_output, its table of hazard ratios. Stops with an error if no exit type has any exits.
